hook_text: Your shop is owed money. But who does your shop owe? That list matters just as much.
clip_script: Ridgeview Hardware sells on credit. It also buys on credit. Suppliers it owes are called creditors: a liability. September. Stock on credit from BuildMart, R8 000: assets up, liabilities up. Stationery on credit, R600: stationery gets used up, so it is an expense. Owner's equity down, liabilities up. A tile cutter on credit, R3 500: equipment it keeps, so assets up, liabilities up. Then Ridgeview pays BuildMart R5 000: bank down, liabilities down, no expense. Add the columns. Assets plus 6 500. Owner's equity minus 600. Liabilities plus 7 100. Minus 600 plus 7 100 is 6 500. Balanced. And Ridgeview owes exactly R7 100.
visual_style: A scale balancing assets against owner's equity and liabilities, tipping and settling with each transaction, supplier logos stacking on the liability side.
pacing: One transaction every few seconds, the scale always settling level, a final total.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and balance Ridgeview's September purchases yourself.
